country.name: Germany
country.context: Germany's Wirtschaftswunder produced a prosperous and orderly society, but one still quietly divided between West and East. Apprenticeships are taken seriously; so is punctuality. The shadow of the 20th century is ever-present in how seriously Germans take politics.

partnerMoments: The standard they hold things to. You. This is part of how they love and it is not always easy.
They still bring you tea when you're working late. You have stopped remarking on it.
The ease of being around them. You notice it most on the days when it isn't there.

log.text: ABBA win Eurovision with "Waterloo." A Swedish group, a song about Napoleon, a sequinned costume. It lands across the continent like a question no one had thought to ask.
Your work reached someone you did not expect. The reaching happened without you.
You are the first in your family to hold a university degree.
You marry Andrea Schulz. The ceremony costs $2,480.
Andrea Schulz tells you and then watches your face, which you understand afterwards was the whole of the test.

The key is yours. You lock and unlock the door three times on the first night just to feel it. The apartment is the size of a large room. There is a mattress on the floor because the bed frame did not fit in the car. One pot. The thing you brought from home sits on the counter because you have not decided where it lives yet.
log.outcome: The call lasts forty minutes. You describe the kitchen. You do not say that it is very quiet here.

log.text: Philipp Hoffmann is born. Everything shifts.
The need to be recognized is still the engine of a lot of your decisions. You are becoming aware of this.
The person you love does not share your religion. Your families have strong opinions about this. Both families do.
log.outcome: Some family members stop speaking to you. The wedding is complicated. The marriage, against expectation, is not.
log.choiceText: Choose your partner — love over family approval

log.text: Stagflation. The economists have a word for it now. The people living it had words for it already.

The first weeks with Philipp Hoffmann. The sleep deprivation is a specific kind of unreality. Your partner is recovering physically, feeding, always doing something. You are learning what you can do that actually helps — which is different from what you thought would help. You are more useful than you feared and less than you hoped. This is probably normal.
Disco. It is everywhere — in the lift, leaking from the car parked outside, in the changing rooms at the pool. You either love it or you are starting to hate it.
The knees give no trouble yet. You have been warned about the knees.

Someone takes you to a bar where no one is performing anything. The music is loud. The strangers nod at you as if you are already known. You have never been in a room that required this little from you.
1973. The petrol queue from the garage to the main road. The odd and even number plates. The Sunday the roads were closed and people walked on them. Everyone learned what the price of oil was.

Philipp Hoffmann says something at dinner that is genuinely, structurally funny — not funny-because-a-child-said-it, funny. There is a pause while you work out whether they know. They do know. You laugh properly, the ugly kind, and they are delighted with themselves and file it away for use later. They will use it later.
SOVIET TROOPS ENTER AFGHANISTAN
The Walkman. A cassette player you hold in your hand and wire into your ears. The commute is never the same after this.
You want to be known and you don't know how to ask for it.
You begin working as a Day Laborer. Starting salary: $2,377/yr.

The fast. However your tradition names it. The physical part is easier than you expected after the first day; the body adjusts. What opens up in the space where ordinary appetite was is harder to describe. Some people call it spiritual clarity. You are not sure what to call it. You notice that the world looks different at sunset when the breaking comes.

65 countries do not go to the Moscow Olympics. The USA boycott, in response to the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, takes their athletes with it. The athletes who spent four years preparing for this have their preparation rendered irrelevant by a diplomatic decision that neither side believes will change anything. The Soviet troops stay in Afghanistan regardless. The athletes train anyway, toward Los Angeles, four years off.
log.context: The 1980 Moscow Olympics were boycotted by 65 countries led by the United States, in response to the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan. US President Jimmy Carter initially threatened athletes who defied the boycott with passport revocation. Many athletes who had spent years preparing did not compete. In 1984, the Soviet Union and 13 allies boycotted the Los Angeles Olympics, officially citing security concerns but widely understood as retaliation. Neither boycott had any measurable effect on the political situations that prompted them.

log.text: STRIKE AT THE LENIN SHIPYARD — SOLIDARITY IS BORN
You have made yourself visible in some arena by now. Two paths clarify: the one that goes further in that direction, and the one that trades visibility for something less public and more real.
log.outcome: You commit. The other path closes, as paths do when you stop looking at them.
log.choiceText: Stay the course. Commit to what you have been building.

log.text: A disease with no name at first, then a name without a treatment. The deaths are concentrated in gay men, intravenous drug users, hemophiliacs. The government is slow to respond. By the time effective treatment arrives, a generation of men has been hollowed out of certain cities. You knew someone. Then you knew several people. Then you stopped counting.
log.context: HIV/AIDS was identified in 1981 in the US, initially among gay men in New York and San Francisco. Reagan did not give a major public AIDS speech until 1987, by which time 20,000 Americans had died. By 1995, AIDS was the leading cause of death for Americans aged 25–44. ACT UP and activist groups pressured for faster drug approval; antiretroviral combination therapy introduced in 1996 transformed AIDS from a terminal diagnosis to a manageable condition for those with access. An estimated 32 million people had died globally by 2020; in Western countries, the epidemic devastated gay male communities in particular, eliminating a generation of artists, activists, and community leaders.

log.text: MARTIAL LAW — TANKS ON THE STREETS OF WARSAW
The sleep is lighter. You hear things at night you did not hear at thirty.

You are thirty-one, and your work has become the thing people say when they say who you are. Some people know your name now. Is it for the thing you wanted? What do you want the next twenty years to hold?
log.outcome: What is already there, you decide. You stop starting things. What exists gets deeper rather than wider.
log.choiceText: Build on what is already there.

log.text: Michael Jackson's Thriller. The album, then the video. Something about the scale of it — global, simultaneous — is different from anything before.
The 3am wake: full consciousness arriving before you want it. The mind presenting its agenda without being asked.
You are promoted to Skilled Laborer. New salary: $4,872/yr.
Your child asks about university. You think about what it meant for you to be the first.
Your neighbor's door opens and closes at two in the morning. You don't know what schedule that belongs to. You have been curious about it for months and will never ask.

A person outside a courthouse, alone, standing very still. Not upset, or past upset. Whatever was decided inside is now a fact and the fact is new and they have not yet integrated it into their understanding of how things are. They are standing with the new fact before they carry it anywhere.
FAMINE IN ETHIOPIA — THE PICTURES FROM KOREM
The Macintosh computer. A screen with a mouse. The way you interact with a machine has changed in a way you cannot yet describe.
Privatisation is the word in the newspapers. The public sector is being reduced in ways that have not yet shown their full consequences.

The new machine arrives on a flatbed with its own engineer, who stays a week. It is run by a panel of buttons and a program on a card, and it does what a whole shift did before it, with one person watching it. The engineer is careful not to look at anyone while he explains this. You watch which of you they choose to be the one person.
log.outcome: You learn. The learning is not pleasant and it takes longer than you expected and you manage it. The job that exists on the other side of it is different from the job you had.
log.choiceText: Adapt — learn what the machine needs that you can provide

log.text: Live Aid. Wembley and JFK Stadium on the same day. A billion and a half people watching the same television feed. Rock music discovering it has a purpose beyond itself.
Sunday is the day with a different shape. The getting-ready, the walk or drive, the greeting of people seen only in this context.

The religious leader you trusted is found to have been taking money. It is not a large amount and that is somehow the worst detail. The institution closes ranks around him. The investigation is slow and the apology, when it comes, is insufficient. You are left with the question of whether the institution and the faith are the same thing, and whether you can separate them.
log.outcome: You find a smaller congregation. Or you practice at home. The faith survives the institution, barely.
log.choiceText: Leave the institution but not the faith

log.text: CHERNOBYL REACTOR EXPLODES — EVACUATION OF PRIPYAT
The thing that happened to your shoulder. The thing has resolved to a certain level and stayed there.
A test comes back with something that needs attention. The doctor speaks carefully.
log.outcome: The habits you build in the next year become permanent.
log.choiceText: Take it seriously — change your life

log.text: The VHS. A film you can watch at home, on your own schedule, paused when you want. The cinema does not disappear, but something shifts in what it means to watch a film.
You are promoted to Foreman. New salary: $12,185/yr.
People in your community start looking to you for leadership. It was not something you sought.
log.outcome: Your world expands. So does your sense of obligation.

log.text: The restaurant was chosen before the price was considered. This continues to be a privilege.
Andrea Schulz is expecting. Neither of you says anything for a moment and then one of you laughs, and it is not entirely a happy laugh, and that is fine.
The marriage is not bad. It is also not what either of you said it would be. Small resentments have settled into the furniture of the relationship. Neither of you mentions them. Both of you know.
log.outcome: Therapy is uncomfortable and useful. Naming things is half the work.

log.text: Markus Hoffmann is born. Everything shifts.

The wall comes down. People are chipping at it with hammers and their hands. A city divided since before you were born becomes one city. You walk through the gap and it is just a street. It is also the most impossible thing you have ever seen.
log.context: The Berlin Wall, thrown up overnight on 13 August 1961, divided East and West Berlin for 28 years; the fortified inner German border divided the two states. On November 9, 1989, the East German government announced citizens could cross freely; crowds immediately overwhelmed the checkpoints. The wall was physically demolished over the following months. Its fall is considered the symbolic end of the Cold War. Germany was formally reunified on October 3, 1990.

log.text: BERLIN WALL FALLS
TIANANMEN SQUARE: TANKS CRUSH THE PROTESTS
The Berlin Wall comes down. The images play on repeat. People hammering at concrete with their bare hands. Something felt impossible three months ago.

Schabowski says it on the television at seven and nobody in the room is sure he meant to. You put your coat on and go to Bornholmer Strasse because staying in seems wrong, and by eleven the barrier is up and nobody has given an order. A man beside you is hitting the concrete with a claw hammer he has clearly brought from a kitchen drawer. The friends who come across in the days after look at the shops the way you look at things you have only been told about.
Two countries become one. The West arrives in the East with its supermarkets and unemployment. Eastern industry closes. Some people gain enormously. Others lose the only world they knew.
log.context: German reunification on October 3, 1990 united West and East Germany under the West German constitution and currency. The economic terms — 1-to-1 currency conversion and rapid privatisation — de-industrialised the East almost overnight. East German unemployment rose to 20–30% within two years as state-owned enterprises collapsed. A generation of East Germans experienced simultaneous democracy, unemployment, and the devaluation of their professional histories. Property restitution claims by pre-war owners created legal conflicts lasting decades. "Ostalgie" — nostalgia for certain aspects of GDR life — emerged as a cultural and political phenomenon.

log.text: GERMANY IS ONE COUNTRY AGAIN
The career was the priority. The other things waited. Some of them are still waiting.
You are visible. People know your name in the relevant arenas. At forty you find yourself wondering what the visibility is hiding, and whether you built it partly for that purpose.
